summary: This diff wires real, previously-missing gates onto the prompt lifecycle state machine (maker-checker, eval-pass-rate threshold, canary duration, PII scan, ownership, ABAC deny, cumulative eval-spend budget) and is well-documented and mostly sound in structure, but it has a confirmed cross-tenant governance bug that undermines the exact safety properties this phase claims to add: prompt_templates/prompt_versions/prompt_eval_runs are explicitly platform-wide tables with no orgId column (confirmed in schema.ts), yet getPromptLifecycleRule() in prompt-governance-service.ts resolves the min_eval_pass_rate/min_canary_duration_hours/eval_daily_budget_usd thresholds through module-rules-resolver.ts's org-override chain, keyed on the acting user's own orgId. setModuleRule() (module-rule-service.ts) lets ANY user with plain 'admin' role (rank 5) set an org-scoped override for moduleKey='prompt_lifecycle' with no allowlist tying moduleKeys to modules that org actually owns. Since these prompt-lifecycle resources are shared across the whole platform (not per-org), a single org's rank-5 admin can set min_canary_duration_hours=0 and min_eval_pass_rate=0 for their own org, after which any veridian_admin (rank 6) in that same org can promote ANY platform-wide prompt template straight to Production, bypassing the canary/eval gates that every other tenant relies on for shared content -- a real privilege/tenant-boundary violation, not a hypothetical. The eval_daily_budget_usd case is a variant of the same root cause: checkPromptEvalBudget() aggregates prompt_eval_runs spend globally (no orgId filter exists on that table) but compares it against a threshold that can be inflated per-org, so one org's override plus usage can also exhaust or distort the shared budget pool for every other org. Given the entire point of this phase is a governance/policy engine, shipping it with a mechanism that lets a lower-privileged role silently weaken platform-wide safety gates is a correctness/security defect that should be fixed (e.g. make prompt_lifecycle rules platform-only, not resolvable through org overrides, or make the underlying resources genuinely org-scoped) before this is held for human sign-off as tier2. Secondary, lower-severity concern: the PII-scan credit-card regex (\b(?:\d[ -]?){13,16}\b) is broad enough to false-positive on ordinary long digit runs (IDs, hashes, dates), which could block legitimate Production promotions -- not a security issue but worth tightening. No .github/workflows/** files are touched in this diff.
issues: Confirmed: prompt_lifecycle business-rule thresholds (min_eval_pass_rate, min_canary_duration_hours, eval_daily_budget_usd) resolve through module-rules-resolver.ts's org-override chain even though prompt_templates/prompt_versions/prompt_eval_runs are platform-wide tables with no orgId column -- any org member with plain 'admin' role (rank 5, below the veridian_admin rank 6 required to actually perform the promotion) can call setModuleRule() to zero out the canary duration and eval-pass-rate gates for their own org, letting a same-org veridian_admin bypass safety gates on ANY platform-wide prompt template, not just content belonging to that org.

Same root cause affects checkPromptEvalBudget(): spend is aggregated globally across prompt_eval_runs (no orgId filter is possible, the table has no such column) but the budget threshold it's compared against can be inflated via a per-org module_rule_configs override, letting one org distort or exhaust a shared platform-wide budget pool for every other org.

checkPromptPolicyDeny() evaluates ABAC deny policies scoped to the acting user's own orgId (abacPolicies.orgId) against a prompt_version resource that has no real org ownership, so the same transition on the same shared prompt version can be allowed or denied incoherently depending on which org's independently-configured policies happen to apply to the actor -- deny-only limits this to over-restriction rather than escalation, but it's still an architectural mismatch between an org-scoped policy engine and a platform-wide resource.

Minor: scanPromptContentForPii's credit-card regex (\b(?:\d[ -]?){13,16}\b) matches almost any 13-16 digit run with optional separators, so it will likely false-positive on legitimate IDs/hashes/concatenated numbers and block valid Production promotions; worth tightening (e.g. Luhn check) even though this is a false-positive/usability risk rather than a security hole.

No test coverage exists for the actual gate-orchestration function (runLifecycleTransitionGates) or the budget-check function -- only the pure PII-scan and dependency-lookup helpers are unit tested; the riskiest new logic (the maker-checker/threshold/ABAC composition, and the cross-tenant issue above) is untested.
